title: Magnitude and extent of arsenic and thallium concentrations in ground water and sediments at the Charleston Naval Complex, North Charleston, South Carolina, 1994-99
citation: Mirecki, J.E., and Falls, W.F., 2002, Magnitude and extent of arsenic and thallium concentrations in ground water and sediments at the Charleston Naval Complex, North Charleston, South Carolina, 1994-99: U.S. Geological Survey Water-Resources Investigations Report 2002-4226, map scale 1:6,000.
notes:
Water-quality report. Appendix 1 (mean arsenic and thallium per well, pages 28-31 and continuing) and tables 1-4 are chemistry statistics with no locations, depths or water levels and were not recorded as observations; the background-well table 2 was also not itemized. Page 7 is an OCR of a photograph (no text). Figure 2 (page 13) is the generalized hydrogeologic section; its thicknesses were recorded from the table text. References outside South Carolina geology (toxicology, analytical methods, regulations) were skipped.
Pages 32-42 continue appendix 1 (mean arsenic and thallium per well, well type and GEOCODE); pages 43-44 are appendix 2 (arsenic in sediment core SYC-1 samples, 10.6 to 142.9 inches below land surface). These are water and sediment chemistry results without locations, screen depths, lithology or water levels, so nothing was recorded in the schema's fields. Pages 45-49 are the back cover and OCR of the two plates (well-location maps of mean arsenic classes); the plate OCR is garbled and holds no geologic values.
Re-read of Appendix 1 (pages 28-42): mean arsenic and thallium concentration per well, one water test per well and constituent. Well number is the observation; well identifier, well type and GEOCODE are in its note; the number of sampling events is in the value note where the text layer gives it. Aquifer is inferred from GEOCODE (U/M upper, NA lower surficial aquifer) for text rows, and taken from the zone heading for rows read from the page image. Cells shown as "—" (no data) are not recorded. The text layer drops some rows and cells near zone headings (p. 29 A038-1D, A039-4D, AGD-2D/3D, BGD wells, C044-1/2; p. 37 G120-3, G636-1 label; several thallium cells; I012-1/2 arsenic); these were read from page images (200 dpi tiles). OCR-garbled well numbers (e.g. 0637-1 for G637-1, 1012-1 for I012-1) are recorded with the likely label, flagged inferred, with the OCR text in the note.
